# People and Fields

There is no single scientific constituency. The political position of a scientist varies by field, profession, employer, status, geography, and relationship to the public.

## People

- Researchers, technicians, and support staff
- Students, postdoctoral researchers, and contingent labor
- Faculty, administrators, and scientific leaders
- Government scientists and regulators
- Industry scientists and entrepreneurs
- Journalists, communicators, and intermediaries

## Fields

- Physical and life sciences
- Medicine and public health
- Engineering and computer science
- Social and behavioral sciences
- Environmental and earth sciences
- Humanities and other neighboring knowledge professions

## Institutions and Boundaries

- Universities, laboratories, agencies, firms, and professional societies
- Credentialed experts and citizen scientists
- Disciplinary differences in evidence, authority, and public exposure
